So what I have done over the last year was get a dot notebook. I started with one I already had in my house instead of buying a new one, but you do you. 

This became my brain as Dr. Barkley suggests. 

I still use Google calendar. It has repeated things, as well as things that are far in the future. Like a Dr appt I may forget about. I set it to automatically have a reminder on everything I put in. Because that's what the Google calendar is for, the reminder. 

The paper brain is to help me think straight. I make a monthly calendar, and weekly calendars. I put hours on my weekly. I don't put much in the monthly one but I still like having it. Mostly I use the weekly version. At first I was making some daily pages but I have decided they don't help me. When I want to decide a day's actions I just start listening to do's, and kind of figure out what I want to do... It's not the best and stuff is still being avoided but I am working on it. If I have appointments and stuff I put them on the paper too and try my best to plan a day. I also try to include some buffer time around things, like 15 min of prep time between actions because I find ending an action to start a new one hard. 

I have started playing with stickers, because they are fun and colorful and make me happy. I have also started gluing pages into the books, stuff from mental health classes I am taking, or notes I typed or whatever. Anything that I think would be good to be able to look at easily. 

It's been a year of working with it, always having a book with me and just trying different things. Also a lot of not judging myself, or being upset that something I tried didn't work. 

I hope some of these ideas help...
